pages.text: You only have a little bit of $(item)Uranium$() from the meteor ritual you performed at the end of the $(item)Combat Simulation$().$(br2)Your current goal is to make it last as long as possible and make some $(item)Nuclear Waste$().$(br2)That will enable you to make the $(item)Почитаемый мировой червь$() which can find more $(item)Uranium$() for you.

pages.title: Nuclear Breeding
pages.notes: Before you can make the most efficient $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() that uses $(item)Molten Salt Plutonium Fuel$() with $(item)D-T Fuel$() (Deuterium & Tritium), you have to breed $(item)Plutonium$() in a breeder reactor.$(br2)You also need to increase your salt production, but that need is not immediate since you have some already.

pages.title: MSR Reactor
pages.notes: The $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() is a state of the art power generation system that will cover all your power needs.$(br2)Since you need a breeder reactor and one producing reactor, you should build at least 2.$(br2)Pull up $(l:portal_hub/4_schematica)Schematica$() to see the bill of materials.

pages.text: Once you have one $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() running, you should store up the $(item)Plutonium Fuel$() and save it for your producing reactor.$(br2)You can run a reactor with just plutonium and molten salt to generate a decent amount of energy. But that will not produce the exotic nuclear waste we need.$(br2)So keep it stocked for now.$(br2)Now lets talk D-T fuel!

pages.title: Deuterium
pages.text: $(item)Deuterium$() is easy to produce. All you need is an $(item)Electrolytic Separator$() that splits $(item)Heavy Water$() into $(item)Deuterium$() and $(item)Oxygen$().$(br2)$(item)Heavy Water$() can be extracted from a body of water with a $(item)Pump$(). The $(item)Pump$() will require a $(item)Filter Upgrade$() to separate heavy water from regular water.

pages.title: Brine
pages.text: Before we can talk about procuring $(item)Tritium$() we have to talk about $(item)Brine$(). $(item)Brine$() is a source of both $(item)Lithium$() and $(item)Salt$().$(br2)If you turn $(item)Brine$() gaseous you can crystallize it into salt, which is what we will do to keep up with our molten salt needs for our $(item)Molten Salt Reactors$().$(br2)$(item)Brine$() is produced in a $(item)Thermal Evaporation Plant$().

pages.title: Brine production
pages.text: There is a small $(item)Thermal Evaporation Plant$() setup you can refer to in $(l:portal_hub/4_schematica)Схематика (Schematica)$() (listed under Mekanism).$(br2)To produce brine you need to pump a metric shit-ton of $(item)Water$() into the plant.$(br2)You will also need to connect a $(item)Resistive Heater$() to one of the valves to sufficiently heat the evaporation plant. For a 12-height plant, the heater will need about 1k RF/t

pages.title: Lithium production
pages.text: To produce $(item)Lithium$(), you must build another $(item)Thermal Evaporation Plant$() that turn $(item)Brine$() into the lithium liquid.$(br2)It can be as small as 3 in height without issue, and you can get away with just giving it 512 RF/t worth of heat with a $(item)Resistive Heater$().$(br2)At this juncture you should probably store the excess brine in a $(item)Black Hole Tank$().

pages.title: Lithium production
pages.text: You may need 2 brine plants to produce $(item)Excess Brine$().$(br2)Siphon some of the excess brine into a $(item)Rotary Condensentrator$() to turn it gaseous. Then pipe the gas to a $(item)Chemical Crystallizer$() that turn in it into salt.$(br2)You probably also want to have a crafter nearby that can directly package the salt into $(item)Salt Blocks$().

pages.title: Tritium production
pages.text: To make the $(item)Tritium$(), first turn the $(item)Liquid Lithium$() gaseous in a $(item)Rotary Condensentrator$().$(br2)Once the lithium is gaseous, pipe it into a $(item)Solar Neutron Activator$(). This will produce $(item)Tritium$() in its gaseous form.

pages.title: D-T Fuel Production
pages.text: To make the D-T fuel, you have to join the $(item)Deuterium$() and the $(item)Tritium$(). This is done in a $(item)Chemical Infuser$() (recipe on the previous page).$(br2)Once it is fused the $(item)D-T Fuel$() is pretty much done!$(br2)Before you send it off to the reactor, run it through a $(item)Rotary Condensentrator$() again to turn it into a liquid.
I am sure you must be winded from reading all that. But it is not really rocket science is it?$(br2)Oh wait, I suppose it kind of is.$(br2)Have fun playing with science!
